findings.what: A declared break of 14 days or more does not withdraw the forecast or the insights at once. r2 values.forecast.withdrawal lists 'declared break of 14 days or more'; r1 F8: 'Withdrawal applies at once', and the insights withdraw on the same conditions. forecastAt has no break check; withdrawalNow covers hold and the warning-sign screen only; insightsWithdrawn likewise. In the week the break is declared (engine ASK) both ranges stay SHOWN ('If you keep training as you have over the last 4 weeks...') and the insights stay ACTIVE until the next week boundary (checked again on Friday of that week). A retroactive break is withdrawn, but only through the calibration (estimate unavailable, then RETURN mode).
findings.why: Sporting: the observed forecast is conditional on continued training and the plan scenario on following the plan. Once the athlete declares two weeks without training, both conditions are known to be false; showing them is the claim the withdrawal exists to remove. It is a decided rule, not a new criterion.
findings.closes: The forecast and the insights are withdrawn from the answer in which a declared break of 14 days or more is on record (declared on or before asOf) and while it is in progress or still to come; afterwards the existing paths (estimate, RETURN mode, zero-credit weeks) apply. Outcome test on the composed entry point: the declaring review, a later day of that week, and a break whose start is in the future. Nothing else changes; no value changes.

findings.what: HOLD weeks are not zero-credit weeks in the composed reading. r2 values.forecast.zeroCreditWeeks includes HOLD; weeksAt marks a week zeroCredit only for the noBandModes (WALK_JOG, RESTART, RETURN). Holds in this engine are review-level (standing F08 holds), not a week mode, so a week spent under a standing hold earns f(a) of whatever was reported and enters the mean of the last weeks. Found by code reading; not reproduced end to end (I did not build a hold followed by a readiness release).
findings.why: If sessions are reported completed during a hold, gain would be credited for a week the decision credits nothing; the other direction (low a lowering the mean) is conservative. The forecast is withdrawn while the hold stands, so the effect is after release only.
findings.probe: code reading: v1-run-forecast-index.mjs weeksAt (zeroCredit: RC.paceRules.noBandModes.includes(modeOf(...))); probes/p07-gzero.mjs shows the pure function credits a zeroCredit week as nothing and leaves it out of the mean
findings.closes: Before the V1X-RUN-FORECAST record, in the same cycle as A-01: a week whose calibration was WITHHELD_HOLD, or that a standing hold covered, is zeroCredit, with an outcome test; or Engineering shows with a test that a week under a hold can never carry a credited report.

findings.what: L-14 checks the planned step (>= 5 min) and each native main step's planning weight (midpoint estimate >= 300 s), not the bout as run. A distance step whose weight is just above 300 s, run FASTER, is a bout under 5 min. In 56 sampled native harder-domain distance steps none falls under 300 s when run FASTER; and under the ADF report contract native reports carry no work pace, so native sessions do not reach a vote today.

findings.what: B-3: the handoff's sanity thresholds are not met (inside the envelope 63.8% against >= 80%; per arm 56.6-67.7% against >= 60%; truth faster than the fast edge 14.8% in the no-response arm against <= 10%). Reproduced exactly. The two central-error criteria are met. In the generator the truth was slower than the slow edge ('assumes no further improvement') in 9-26% of cases per arm.
findings.why: The envelope was never a probability interval: its slow edge is the V1RC current estimate itself and its width is the V1RC single-source margin; r1 C5 and r2 A2 record no measured coverage, the interval is labelled PLAUSIBILITY_ENVELOPE, probabilistic false, calibrated false, and no copy may state a coverage. The slow-side misses come from the V1RC estimate the forecast starts from, not from anything phase B adds. The result confirms the abstentions; it does not block a synthetic candidate. The generator and the values must not be tuned to pass.

V5.ruling: COUNTED_WITH_CREDIT_ZERO ('ZERO', the candidate's provisional value) — this answer prevails
V5.reason: r2's own last credit rule gives 0 to a report with no recorded extent, and the forecast's adherence is a proxy for the stimulus received that must err low (A6). Excluding the session from both sides would let an athlete with many unreadable sessions keep a high weekly adherence from the few readable ones: the over-credit direction. A later correction reclassifies the session. Credit 0 only slows the fast edge and feeds nothing else.

L-1.reason: A conflicted row is no readable execution; same reading as V5. The engine's completed is false for a conflicted row, so it never reaches credit 1.

L-2.reason: The credit measures the dose received; a session the plan skipped and did not move is dose not received, whatever the cause, and counting it errs low. A moved session counts once, where it lives; an optional one only when reported. G03 semantics stay with Product/UX + Data (C13).

L-3.reason: The smaller usable distance over the target is the conservative extent; extentFraction is never read (grep: one comment only). Closes SSCTR-RWS-E-03 for this phase's readers.

L-4.reason: ADF section 6 and r1 F2: an unstated class reads EXPERIENCED, the smallest ceiling; reading the intake's stored NOVICE would overstate the gain of someone who said nothing. Verified end to end (p03 S6).

L-5.reason: The evidence boundary (admitted record, A6 credit, pace admission) exists only through the run-format entry point; without V1X-RUN-NATIVE there is no conforming reading.

L-6.reason: Matches A1's one condition and 'recompute at the week boundary only'.

L-7.reason: Eligibility read as the calibration read the reference; voiding a pair across a gap leaves the prior, which is wider, never more confident (A-08).

L-8.reason: A4's intent is a frozen range never shown altered; recomputing from the record and withholding it when anything that week read has changed since, or a break was declared since, is stricter.

L-9.how: Accept not applying the 112-day window and 'estimate unavailable' to the insights: those guard a projection, and the insights read the band of each session's own week and stand without an event estimate. But a declared break of 14 days or more must withdraw the insights at once too (r1 F8 'the same conditions'); see SSCTR-RFC-A-01.

L-10.reason: The decision names no action for STABLE or MIXED; NONE suggests nothing, and the state itself is shown.

L-11.reason: Checking the lapse at every boundary from 56 days is stricter than 'the first boundary' and cannot keep a revision longer.

L-12.reason: The V1 vocabulary has no GOOD: device quality is OK, POOR or absent (v1-run-history). OK is the positive assessment; absent is 'merely not poor' and does not count, which is what A3 meant.
L-12.condition: Before any V1X-PACE-REVISION record: only a device-authored quality counts (the app never says OK for a device: QRE-RWS-F-01 closure (a), SSCTR-RWS-F-02), and Data confirms the HealthKit mapping sets OK only on a positive assessment (E4).

L-13.reason: Reported effort is the athlete's word, not pace evidence; ending the revision and blocking an offer on a harder-than-cue report even with the pace withheld is the conservative reading of A3.

L-14.reason: Planned step >= 5 min and every native main step >= 300 s closes SSCTR-RWS-A-04 for this phase's readers, which never rely on paceEvidence === true. A-04 stays open for any other reader of the flag. Residual: SSCTR-RFC-A-05.

limitsOfTheProjection: Held: slow edge always the current estimate (every example and every composed week); O never added (g = U + F); the reference week credited at the reference (A1-1, A1-2); two ranges, observed first, plan scenario never the headline while the observed is SHOWN, coincidence rule; the plan scenario can never be shown alone while an observed forecast is available (its low is never above the observed low); marathon only as the current estimate with no range kind and no goal relation; 112-day window; race week: frozen observed low-high only, dated, after the V1RC caution, never on race day, never with a goal relation, every not-shown cause; goal relation on rounded edges, inclusive, neutral, never the central; adherence by extent never intensity; each g = 0 rule (marathon, slowdown >= 3%, Q8 down); withdrawals: hold, clinical route, screen, modes, completion race, after the race date, race week, window, estimate unavailable, experience NONE, boundaries not enabled, marathon above 6:00:00, with the exception of SSCTR-RFC-A-01.
uncertaintyAndUnavailable: No more precision or confidence than decided: confidence LOW whenever a gain is applied, else the current tier capped at MODERATE; outward rounding of V1RC; no z, percentage or probability beside a range (the basis text says 'not a probability', as decided); thin evidence gives TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW or a typed UNAVAILABLE with the V1RC reason and the decided routes, never a fabricated value; a non-current personal best is HISTORICAL_BEST in V1RC and never capacity; aged evidence is PRESUMED with a reduced tier and the forecast then goes TOO_UNCERTAIN (B-1).
paceInsights: Observational: with the insights on, every key of the run formats and the calibration hash are unchanged (p03 S8); a single easy run, or several fast easy runs, change neither the forecast nor any insight state (p03 S3; easy runs are no insight domain). Classification, exceptional rule, states and actions as decided (PI-1, PR-2, PR-3). The revision: every offer condition, the step, the 3% total, every ending and the lapse reproduce (p02); race-pace domains are never revised (PR-2, PR-3). With no enabling record of its own, V1X-PACE-REVISION is INERT: nothing offered or recorded, the effective band is the V1RC band, nothing re-sized (p03 S8, and the default authority approves nothing).
